wiring.connector: opener low-voltage terminals (LiftMaster/Chamberlain red / white / common)
wiring.notes: Reached through a ratgdo/Konnected bridge board wired in parallel with the wall console: Ground, Control (data) and Obstruction. The board's ESP UART drives the line.

messages.name: door_command (toggle)
messages.notes: Emulated wall-panel button press: opens a closed door / closes an open one (single-button toggle). Carried in the Security+ packet with the current rolling code; the bridge increments and persists the counter.

messages.name: status_report
messages.notes: Security+ 2.0 only: door position (open/closed/opening/closing/stopped), obstruction-sensor state, light state, motion and lockout. Security+ 1.0 status is limited.

bus.notes: Two physical generations. Security+ 2.0 (yellow learn button) is the documented link above: 9600 baud 8N1, 19-byte packets, the board authenticates as a wall panel and gets bidirectional status. Security+ 1.0 (purple/orange/red) instead runs 1200 baud 8E1 with simpler byte commands and limited status. The rolling-code codec (Sec+ 2.0: 40-bit fixed + 28-bit rolling, obfuscated by bit-reverse -> base-3 -> 2-bit remap + permutation; counter +1/press) is fully implemented in argilo/secplus and ratgdo — this spec points at those rather than restating the bit math. Security+ 3.0 (white learn button) is not on the wire at all (encrypted BLE) and cannot be bridged.

discovery.none: Nothing to discover: the opener speaks Security+ over its low-voltage wall-control terminals and has no radio a phone can hear. The aftermarket bridge wired to those terminals is what appears on the network, and it is discovered by its own spec (see ratgdo.yaml).

device.name: Chamberlain/LiftMaster Garage Opener (Security+ wired, via bridge)
device.notes:
Chamberlain's MyQ CLOUD product has no local control (see the research-notes/myq-cloud-hub dud: the MyQ Wi-Fi hub is outbound-cloud-only, verified 2026-08-14 with all local ports closed). The garage OPENER itself, however, is locally controllable — not over the network, but by wiring an aftermarket bridge board (ratgdo, GPL-2.0; or Konnected blaQ) to the opener's low-voltage wall-control terminals. The board impersonates a wall-console and speaks the opener's native Security+ wire protocol, exposing local control + full door status over ESPHome / MQTT with no cloud and no MyQ. This spec documents that wired protocol; the transport is UART because that is what the bridge speaks to the opener. The bridge's NETWORK-facing API (what a phone app actually talks to) is documented separately in ratgdo.yaml.
GENERATION GATE (identify by the learn-button color before committing): - Security+ 1.0 (purple / orange / red learn button): wired UART
  1200 baud, 8E1. ~32-bit rolling + ~32-bit fixed code as 40 ternary
  symbols; counter increments by 3 per press. Bridgeable but "experimental"
  in ratgdo, limited status.
- Security+ 2.0 (yellow learn button): wired UART 9600 baud, 8N1, 19-byte
  packets. 40-bit fixed + 28-bit rolling (+ optional 32-bit supplemental),
  counter +1 per press. The rolling code is obfuscated (bit-reverse ->
  base-3 -> 2-bit remap + permutation) — the "obfuscated serial signal"
  that defeats a plain relay. Best target: mature firmware, bidirectional
  status (door position, obstruction, light, motion, lockout). The bridge
  persists the rolling-code counter across reboots to stay in sync.
- Security+ 3.0 (WHITE learn button, Nov 2025+): NOT locally controllable
  by anyone. Accessory comms moved to encrypted BLE; the wall-button wires
  carry power only, no data to tap. Uncracked. Out of scope — flag and
  stop.

NO LEARN STEP FOR THE WIRED LINK: the opener's learn button enrols RADIO remotes and keypads, not wall controls. A Sec+ 2.0 bridge picks a random client ID (the 40-bit fixed field) and the opener accepts its packets as long as the rolling counter keeps moving forward; Sec+ 1.0 wired commands carry no rolling code at all. See device.pairing.
SAFETY: this actuates a heavy motorised door. Control is a single toggle that opens or closes; a bridge with door-position status should gate commands on the current state. The Security+ rolling code is anti-replay, not authorisation — anyone who can reach the wall-control wires can drive the door, so physical access to the terminals is the only gate.
SIBLING HARDWARE (VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-19): a LAN sweep found a SECOND Chamberlain-family device alongside the closed-port MyQ hub from the research-notes/myq-cloud-hub dud — a MyQ Smart Garage Control hub, model MYQ-G0401 ("SMART GARAGE CONTROL,GEN3,BLE,CH" per its own identity response; firmware 1.10), at 192.168.1.50 (MAC 24:18:c6:aa:bb:cc). Unlike the 2026-08-14 hub (all local ports closed), this unit answers on :80: an UNAUTHENTICATED JSON identity endpoint GET /jabout (returns product/model string, brand, MyQ serial, AP name, firmware version, MAC, joined SSID, RSSI and uptime — no credentials requested) and a Wi-Fi setup web UI at / (GET only — HEAD / returns 404 because HEAD is not implemented, which explains an earlier "404 on /" observation; /myq.js and /brand.js reference setup.myqdevice.com). Other /j* paths 404; the LAN surface is minimal and read-only — there is NO local door control: actual control remains MyQ cloud + the hub's BLE link to the opener, so the wired bridge story above is unchanged and still the only local control path. Captured responses (myq_jabout.json, myq_index.html, with checksums) are archived in the maintainers' private research workspace, not committed here.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The opener's LEARN button is not part of this link. It opens the opener's window for enrolling radio remotes, keypads and MyQ accessories, and a wired bridge can trigger that same window itself (ratgdo's Learn switch sends the wall-panel learn command), which is a reason to keep the bridge's network side locked down.

exclusivity.recovery: If the opener ignores a Sec+ 2.0 bridge it used to obey, the bridge's rolling counter has fallen behind what the opener last saw from that client ID — typically after a reflash restored an old counter. Use the bridge's Sync, move the rolling-code counter well forward, or give it a new client ID (ratgdo: bump the Client ID number, or reinstall with Erase, which generates a fresh one). Two bridges sharing one client ID will keep desynchronising each other; the wall console itself can stay.

pairing.notes: Nothing a person does at the opener authorises the wired bridge. On Security+ 2.0 the bridge chooses its own client ID for the fixed field and sends rolling-code packets on the wall-control line; the opener acts on any well-formed packet whose counter is ahead of the last one it saw from that ID. That rolling code is anti-replay, not authorisation — esphome-ratgdo has no pairing step, simply queries status on boot and jumps its counter forward if the opener stays silent, and a project collaborator's answer in its issue tracker is that no pairing is needed. Security+ 1.0 wired commands are plain bytes with no rolling code. So physical access to the wall-control terminals is the whole gate. The opener does report a count of wall controls it knows about (ratgdo's Paired Devices), which suggests it records client IDs as it hears them, but nothing has to be enrolled first. Security+ 3.0 (white learn button) moved accessories to encrypted BLE and is out of reach.

credentials.notes: No network credential crosses to the opener. The Sec+ 2.0 rolling code is the only thing resembling authentication, and the bridge seeds it itself (random client ID, counter persisted on the board); no button press at the opener is involved.
stored_on_device: Security+ rolling-code counter (persisted on the bridge board)

factory_reset.description:
Two operations behind one button, and the difference is how many times you do it. A single hold erases the radio codes — the answer to "I sold the house and want the previous owner's remotes dead". The triple sequence is the full reset that also takes the network side with it.
Do the second one only if you mean it: every remote and keypad in the household stops working at the same moment, and if the only way back into the garage was one of them, that is a problem to solve before pressing rather than after.
factory_reset.effect: Erases every paired remote control and keyless entry code from the opener. On WiFi models the triple sequence additionally clears MyQ accessories and the built-in gateway's settings. Everything erased has to be reprogrammed, including remotes that were working fine.

procedures.basis: Chamberlain/LiftMaster dealer and alarm-monitoring documentation for the WiFi opener range, which give the same hold and the same LED behaviour.
procedures.name: LEARN button held once — erase all remotes and keypad codes

steps.action: Press and hold the LEARN button on the opener until the LEARN LED goes out — about six to ten seconds.
steps.expect: All remote and keyless-entry codes are erased.

procedures.basis: Chamberlain/LiftMaster factory-reset instructions for the WiFi garage door opener range.
procedures.indicator: Three quick beeps after the third hold.
procedures.name: LEARN button held three times — full factory reset (WiFi models)

steps.action: Press and hold the LEARN button until the LEARN LED goes out.
Immediately hold it again until the LED goes out.
Immediately hold it a third time until the LED goes out.
steps.expect: Three quick beeps — codes, MyQ accessories and the gateway settings are all erased.

methods.description: Install a Security+ bridge board (ratgdo/Konnected) on the opener's wall-control terminals; it exposes local control over ESPHome/MQTT.

steps.action: Identify the opener's Security+ generation by learn-button color (purple/orange/red = 1.0, yellow = 2.0, white = 3.0 unsupported).
Wire the bridge board to Ground / Control / Obstruction terminals (parallel to the wall console).
Power the board; on Sec+ 2.0 it queries the opener and brings its rolling-code counter into sync on its own. No learn-button press is needed.
steps.expect: The board reports door status and can open/close; the physical wall button keeps working.

setup.notes: Requires aftermarket hardware: a ratgdo or Konnected board wired to the opener's wall-control terminals (Ground, Control/data, Obstruction — on LiftMaster/Chamberlain Sec+ 2.0 the red/white/common terminals). The board runs in parallel with the existing wall button. No learn-button press is needed for the wired link (see device.pairing). Confidence medium: the wired UART parameters and wall-panel emulation are proven by ratgdo/Konnected firmware in the field, but this project has not driven hardware.

rejoin.notes: The bridge board joins the home Wi-Fi like any ESPHome device; the opener pairing is independent of the network.

covers: Door position, obstruction, light and motion status (Security+ 2.0)
not_covered: Any local control via MyQ hubs — the MYQ-G0401's LAN surface is identity/setup only; door control stays cloud + BLE
local_access.summary: No local interface on the stock opener/MyQ hub; local control requires an aftermarket wired bridge (ratgdo/Konnected) speaking Security+ 1.0/2.0. Blocked on Security+ 3.0 (encrypted BLE, uncracked). The sibling MyQ Smart Garage Control hub MYQ-G0401 (verified live 2026-08-19) exposes only a read-only identity endpoint (/jabout) and a Wi-Fi setup UI on :80 — useful for identification, not control.
